fact: Gabon Review reports that the Mairie Centrale d'Oyem is among the administrations of Oyem already on the Réseau de l'Administration Gabonaise, a public fibre-optic network dedicated to the administration that ANINF, the state's digital infrastructure agency, has brought into service there; the activation is undated, so the date is the article's.

Gabon Review says the RAG connection at Oyem improves the working conditions of the public services and prepares the progressive integration of new digital uses in the administrations concerned; it names no system the town hall's staff work in, and the date is the article's.

Gabon Review names one local government office on the RAG, the Mairie Centrale d'Oyem in Woleu-Ntem, beside the town's police station and courthouse, and says activation will continue to other administrations of the locality and then to other public entities; it gives no total of communes connected or to be connected, and the date is the article's.

Gabon Review describes the RAG as a public network dedicated to the administrations and controlled by the State, activated at Oyem by ANINF, which it calls the State's operational arm for public digital infrastructure; it states no cost and no source of finance, and the date is the article's.

Gabon Review reports that the RAG fibre infrastructure at Oyem, installed in 2010 and inactive since, has been brought into service by ANINF and already serves the Mairie Centrale d'Oyem; the activation is undated, so the date is the article's.
